title: MemDLM: Memory-Enhanced DLM Training
claim: Our method consistently beats the standard baseline on long-context retrieval tasks across backbones and context lengths, with large average gains.
layout: 5 columns, 2 backbone rows, plus a summary bar panel on right
description: A grid of grouped bar charts comparing Standard MDLM (gray) and MemDLM (blue) on long-context needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks. Two rows correspond to two backbones, LLaDA-MoE on top and LLaDA2.1 on the bottom. Four columns cover RULER-MV, RULER-VT, RULER-CWE and BABILong. Each subplot has pairs of bars at 2K, 4K or 8K context length, and the blue bar is nearly always taller than the gray one. A fifth tall panel on the right, titled Avg. Absolute Improvement, shows labeled bars for each task and backbone. The largest gain is 23.92 on RULER-VT for LLaDA2.1. A legend sits at the top left, and the y-axis is Score. The eye goes first to the blue bars and then to the improvement panel.
caption: Needle-in-a-Haystack results overview. Gray bars denote Standard MDLM and blue bars denote MemDLM. Left: detailed results on RULER-MV, RULER-VT, RULER-CWE, and BABILong for the LLaDA-MoE-7B-A1B-Base and LLaDA2.1-mini backbones. Right: mean absolute improvement of MemDLM over Standard MDLM for each task, averaged across the evaluated context lengths within each backbone.
abstract: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) offer attractive advantages over Auto-Regressive (AR) models, such as full-attention parallel decoding and flexible generation. However, standard DLM training uses a static, single-step masked prediction objective that never exposes the model to the progressive denoising dynamics of inference, and forces all contextual information to be maintained purely through token-space attention, which becomes increasingly diluted as context length grows. We propose MemDLM (Memory-Enhanced DLM), which introduces a second memory channel by embedding a simulated denoising trajectory into training via Bi-level Optimization. An inner loop updates a set of fast weights, forming a Parametric Memory that captures the local trajectory experience, while an outer loop updates the base model conditioned on this memory. By offloading part of the memorization burden from token-space attention to parameter space, MemDLM yields faster convergence, stronger long-context representations, and lower training loss, even when the fast weights are discarded at inference time. Re-enabling the inner loop at inference provides an additional prompt-specific adaptation effect, where the Parametric Memory acts as an emergent in-weight retrieval mechanism on challenging Needle-in-a-Haystack tasks. Code: https://github.com/JarvisPei/MemDLM.
